 Damian W. Betebenner Projection Models are Superior to SGP

Main Points
 The SGP Model is intended to allow stakeholders to answer three
 questions simultaneously:
 What is? What is a student’s growth is answered in a
 norm-referenced fashion using student growth
 percentiles.
 What should be? What should a student’s growth be to reach or
 maintain desired levels of achievement is a
 criterion-referenced question and is answered using
 student growth projections.
 What is reasonable? Because SGPs are percentiles and are
 conditional probabilities, we implicitly understand
 what is a modest growth goal versus what is an
 ambitious growth goal.
 One needs both norms and criteria to fully understand all
 phenomena, including student growth.
 Thus, to answer the debate question, one needs both student
 growth percentiles (norms) and student growth projections (criteria)
 to make sense.
